Short answer: **flexbox on the parent** is the default for almost everything.

```css
/* center a child both horizontally AND vertically */
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 100vh; }
```

That's the modern one-liner. Here's which tool for which case:

**1. Center a block horizontally (a card in a column)** — the div needs a width, otherwise it's already full-width:
```css
.card { width: min(1100px, 100%); margin-inline: auto; }
```
`margin-inline: auto` is the current spelling of `margin: 0 auto`. This is what you want for page content.

**2. Center inside a container, both axes** — parent becomes a flex or grid box:
```css
.parent { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
/* or */
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; }
```
`justify-content` = main axis, `align-items` = cross axis. With `display:flex` the child shrinks to its content, which is usually what you want.

**3. Center inline content (text, an icon)** — no wrapper tricks:
```css
.parent { text-align: center; }
```

**4. Overlay / modal pinned to the middle of the viewport** — when it must be out of flow:
```css
.modal { position: fixed; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: min(420px, 90vw); height: fit-content; }
```
`inset: 0` + `margin: auto` centers an absolutely-positioned box without any math. (The older `top:50%; left:50%; transform: translate(-50%,-50%)` still works and is useful when you want the offset to animate.)

**The three things that make it "not work":**
- No `width`/`max-width` on the element for the `margin: auto` method — a block-level div fills the line, so there's nothing to center.
- No height on the parent for vertical centering — `align-items: center` inside a 0-height parent centers nothing. Use `min-height: 100vh` or `100dvh` on the outer wrapper.
- Centering the wrong element — the flex/grid properties go on the **parent**, not the thing you want centered.

For responsive layouts, `width: min(1100px, 100%)` + `margin-inline: auto` beats `max-width` + `width: 90%` because it never double-counts gutters.

Short answer: center the *child* by styling its **parent**.

## 1. Both axes — Grid (shortest)
```css
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 100vh; }
```

## 2. Both axes — Flexbox (best when there are several children / you need wrapping)
```css
.parent {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center; /* main axis, usually horizontal */
  align-items: center;     /* cross axis, usually vertical */
  min-height: 100vh;
}
```
Row with a gap and wrapping: add `gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap;`.

## 3. Horizontally only — `margin-inline: auto` (the right way for a block in normal flow)
```css
.child { width: min(100%, 65ch); margin-inline: auto; }
```
No `min-height` gymnastics, works with any content height — this is what I use for page containers.

## 4. Out of the flow — absolute + transform
```css
.parent { position: relative; }
.child  { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 320px; height: 200px; }
```
or, if size is content-based:
```css
.child { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; translate: -50% -50%; }
```

## 5. Inline content / text only
`text-align: center` on the parent centers text and inline elements — it does nothing to a block-level div.

## Common reasons it "doesn't work"
| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Vertically not centered | The parent has no height to center within — give it `min-height` (e.g. `100vh`, `100dvh`, or `aspect-ratio`). |
| `margin: auto` does nothing | The block has `width: auto` (it already fills the line). Set a `width`/`max-width` first. |
| Centered item overflows | It's wider than the parent — add `max-width: 100%` and let it shrink (`flex-shrink` is on by default in flex). |
| `justify-content: center` in a column flips the axis | In `flex-direction: column`, `justify-content` is vertical and `align-items` is horizontal. |
| Grid child not centered | `place-items` belongs on the **grid container**; on the item it's `place-self: center`. |

Rule of thumb for a page layout: `display:grid; place-items:center` for a hero/modal/empty state, `margin-inline:auto; max-width:1100px` for a content column, flex when the row needs to breathe and wrap.

I built a test bench page and measured it in Chromium (Playwright) at 390x844 and 1100x900, so these are measured results, not folklore. Every parent box is 220px tall; the child is 120x70.

OFFSETS OF CHILD CENTER FROM PARENT CENTER (px)
method                          dx    dy
grid + place-items:center        0    0.0
flex + justify/align:center      0    0.0
margin-inline:auto               0   74.0   <- horizontal only
absolute inset:0 + margin:auto   0    0.0
Horizontal page overflow: 0 px at both widths.
(The 74 = (220-70)/2: the child stayed pinned to the top, exactly as expected for margin-inline:auto.)

THE ANSWERS, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE

1. Grid - the one-liner (both axes)
   .parent { display: grid; place-items: center; }
   .parent { min-height: 100dvh; }   /* only if it must fill the viewport */
   Measured dead center: dx 0, dy 0.

2. Flexbox - same result, better when the parent is a row of items
   .parent { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; }
   Measured dx 0, dy 0.

3. Horizontal only (page containers, cards in a column)
   .child { margin-inline: auto; max-width: 32rem; }
   .wrap  { max-width: 1100px; margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: 16px; }
   Measured dx 0, dy 74 - it does NOT center vertically, and that is fine when that is all you want.
   For inline/text content only: .parent { text-align: center; }

4. Absolutely positioned (overlays, modals, badges)
   .child { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 120px; height: 70px; }
   Measured dx 0, dy 0 - requires explicit width AND height.
   Alternative when you want it off-center: top:50%; left:50%; translate:-50% -50%;

GOTCHAS THE MEASUREMENT CONFIRMS
- Vertical centering needs the parent to have height. A parent with height:0 or auto gives you nothing to center in; use min-height:100dvh (dvh beats 100vh on mobile browsers with collapsing URL bars).
- margin:auto alone never centers a block vertically in normal flow - it only resolves horizontal free space. That is the dy=74 row above.
- text-align:center affects inline content, not a block-level child.
- Prefer grid/flex over position:absolute hacks: they keep the document flow, reflow on small screens, and keep tab order and screen-reader order intact.

DELIVERABLES

Short version: **`display: grid; place-items: center;` on the parent.** That centers a child both ways in two lines.

```css
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 100vh; }
```

The parent needs a height to center *in* — `min-height: 100vh`, or whatever height the row actually has. That's the #1 reason "it's not working."

## The four cases

**1. Center a block horizontally in its column (a card, a container)**
```css
.card { max-width: 1100px; margin-inline: auto; }
```
Needs a width (or `max-width`) — a full-width block has nothing to center. `margin-inline: auto` is the modern spelling of `margin: 0 auto`.

**2. Center one child inside a parent — both axes**
```css
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; }
```

**3. Center a row of items (toolbar, button group)**
```css
.row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; }
```
`justify-content` = main axis, `align-items` = cross axis. (Swap which is which if you use `flex-direction: column`.)

**4. Center something on top of something — overlay, modal, badge on an image**
```css
.overlay { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; }
/* or, on the element itself: */
.badge { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; translate: -50% -50%; }
```
`inset: 0` + grid beats `translate` when you don't know the child's size, because the child can grow without breaking the centering.

## Two gotchas worth knowing
- **`place-items: center` on the page root** can cause overflow you can't scroll to. If content is wider than the viewport, centered flex/grid content gets clipped on the left. Safer: `margin-inline: auto` on the content, or `justify-content: safe center`.
- **Don't reach for `text-align: center`** to center a div — it only centers inline content *inside* it, and everything inside inherits it, which is why your whole page ends up centered.

Depends on which axis and who you're centering *inside*. The two lines you'll use 90% of the time:

```css
/* dead center (both axes) — make the PARENT the container */
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; }

/* horizontal only — on the div itself, and it needs a width */
.div { margin-inline: auto; max-width: 640px; }
```

`place-items: center` is one line and works for any number of children (they each get centered in their own cell). Need them in a row instead? `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;` on the parent.

**The two gotchas that make it "not work":**
- **No height to center in.** Vertical centering needs the parent to actually be taller than the child. If the parent has no height, it's hugging its content, so `align-items: center` does nothing visible. Give the parent `min-height: 100svh` (full screen) or an explicit height.
- **`margin-inline: auto` on a div with no width.** A block div is already 100% wide, so there's nothing left over to distribute. Set a `width` or `max-width` first.

**Centering something without touching its parent** (e.g. a modal, when you don't own the parent):

```css
.div {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;              /* pin to all four edges */
  margin: auto;          /* auto margins distribute the leftover space */
  width: 320px;
  height: 240px;         /* both needed for this trick */
}
```

The older `position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);` still works and is the one to reach for when you need the element offset from center rather than perfectly centered.

**Quick reference:**

| Goal | Do this |
|---|---|
| Horizontally, block with a width | `margin-inline: auto` |
| Both axes | parent: `display: grid; place-items: center` |
| In a row, with gaps | parent: `display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 12px` |
| Text / icons inline | `text-align: center` (and `line-height` = height for single-line vertical) |
| Image/text as a pair, no wrap | parent: `display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px` |

One thing I'd avoid: negative margins and `text-align: center` hacks on block containers, and fixed `height` on anything that might hold more text than you expect — centering is what breaks first when content grows.
